html:
The Botswana Meat Commission was set up in 1966 to run the country's abattoir at Lobatse and sell Botswana's beef abroad, especially to Europe.

Cattle had long been the wealth and status of the Tswana, kept at distant cattle posts and loaned among families, as in the chiefdom of Khama III. Before diamonds, beef was the country's main export, and the commission won a protected market in Europe under trade deals for former colonies.

Veterinary fences built across the Kalahari to keep out foot-and-mouth disease protected the trade but cut wildlife migration routes. Cattle remain a core of rural life and of the wealth of the elite, alongside diamonds in Botswana.
sum: The Botswana Meat Commission was set up in 1966 to run the country's abattoir at Lobatse and sell Botswana's beef abroad, especially to Europe.
